summary: Verified the New Starter Portal 'returning-user login' bug fix end-to-end. Backend: 9/9 pytest cases pass (invite status flip false→true, first-time accept-invite 200, repeat accept-invite 409, login 401 on wrong pw / 200 on correct pw, /me works with the returning JWT, unknown-token 404). Frontend (Playwright at /new-starter/<token>): first-time card shows 'Welcome to Pulse Fitness' + 'Create a password' + 'Enter my portal'; after clicking Log out the same card correctly re-renders as 'Welcome back, UIT' + 'Your password' + 'Log in' (core bug fix — no longer offers to Create a password); wrong password shows 'Incorrect password — please try again.' via nsp-error and does NOT enter the portal; correct password logs back into nsp-portal.

issues: A global 'Your session has expired — Sign in again' toast overlays the recruit portal after re-login (likely bleeding in from the main-app AuthContext even though the recruit portal is a separate white-branded page). Cosmetic only — did not block interactions in the automated run — but recruits will see it and may be confused. Recommend suppressing the main-app session-expired toast on the /new-starter/* route.

action_items: Optional: hide the main-app 'Session expired — Sign in again' toast on the /new-starter/* route so the recruit portal stays cleanly white-branded.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/staff_onboarding_wizard.py: invite_status() correctly gates 'accepted' on BOTH invite.status=='accepted' AND user.password existing — good defence-in-depth against a partial state where the invite row was flipped but the user record wasn't.

accept-invite now short-circuits with 409 only when status=='accepted' AND user has a password; if for any reason the user row is missing/blank it will (re)set the password. This is a sensible fallback but worth an audit_log entry when the fallback path fires so ops can spot corrupt invites.
Frontend: sessionStorage key is per-token (nsp:<token>) — good, doesn't leak across different recruit links on the same browser. logout() clears password state as well.

Frontend uses `returning = !!inviteInfo?.accepted` — if the /invite/{token} call fails, inviteInfo stays null and the UI falls back to first-time copy. That's the safer default (a POST to accept-invite for an already-accepted token now returns 409, so no silent reset) but worth noting so future changes preserve that ordering.
